Attached is Velaria's round-1 redline of Redwood's DPA (Velaria_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). Key items flagged by our counsel:
- Cross-border transfers: we proposed a narrow set of SCCs + an obligation to notify if a transfer mechanism changes.

- Audit scope: limited to information security and access logs for the relevant services (no broad source-code audit).
- Retention & deletion: a 12-month maximum for customer data after termination, with narrow carveouts for aggregated telemetry.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on these points so we can route to procurement and schedule DocuSign? Our legal team (cc'd Grant) is available for a short call Friday if helpful.

Anand — thanks for sending and for the clear summary. We've reviewed the redline at a high level and attached Redwood's annotated draft (Redwood_counsel_annotated.docx) with callouts. High-level positions from Redwood counsel:

1) Subprocessor notice and objection
- We are willing to provide advance notice of new subprocessors and an objection window, but 60 days is longer than our standard operational cadence. Proposed change: 30 calendar days notice for new subprocessors (by email to privacy@velaria.com), with the right to object in writing. If Velaria objects, we'll engage in good-faith remediation or offer a reasonable alternative.

2) Cross-border transfers
- We accept use of the EU SCCs for EEA transfers. We request language that allows Redwood to rely on approved mechanisms (SCCs, EU adequacy, or other lawful transfer mechanism) and to update the transfer mechanism with notice. We'll add a brief change-notify clause (30 days) rather than an ongoing reconsent for minor operational changes.

3) Audit scope
- Agree that audits should be scoped to data relevant to the services provisioned to Velaria. We cannot permit source-code review or on-prem system access. We propose a mutually agreed audit plan and a remote evidence-based process (logs, configs, SOC2 report excerpts).

4) Retention & deletion
- The 12-month post-termination retention for customer data is acceptable for production data; however, security/audit logs and legal hold obligations may require narrower exceptions. Proposed compromise language: primary customer data deleted within 12 months; a limited retention carveout for logs/telemetry for up to 18 months for security/investigations, with obligation to minimize and redact.

Next steps: Rishi (cc'd) will upload a short redline of these items and a subprocessor matrix for transparency. If Velaria is comfortable, we can prepare an execution copy and initiate DocuSign (we typically send via DocuSign unless you prefer AdobeSign).

For scheduling: we can do a 30-minute call Friday 10:00–10:30 PT to resolve any open technical points.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Anand/Grant — hi, Rishi from Redwood Legal. A few technical notes and proposed language snippets to help counsel triage the redline. I'm pasting the important bits inline and attaching our subprocessor inventory (.csv) for the current roster.

A. Subprocessor notification/objection
- Proposed language (replace Velaria 60-day ask): "Redwood will provide notice of the addition of any Subprocessor that will process EEA personal data at least thirty (30) days prior to such Subprocessor commencing processing. Customer may raise a written objection within thirty (30) days of receipt of notice, specifying reasonable grounds. If the parties cannot resolve the objection, Customer may require Redwood to suspend processing of Customer personal data by the Subprocessor for Customer's accounts until the parties have agreed on appropriate safeguards; provided that Redwood may propose an alternative Subprocessor or technical measure."

B. Transfer mechanisms / SCCs
- We recommend a clause allowing Redwood to apply standard SCCs and update the Annex with the chosen transfer mechanism. Suggested text: "The parties agree that transfers of personal data from the EEA may be governed by the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (processor-processor or controller-processor as applicable) or other lawful mechanisms. Redwood may adopt an updated transfer mechanism to comply with law by providing Customer with written notice."

C. Audit / evidence scope
- Remote evidence preferred. Proposed: "Customer audits shall be limited to a review of Redwood's security policies, SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, relevant access logs and configurations for the Customer's environment. Onsite audits are subject to advanced notice and are limited to document review; no access to source code or operational consoles will be permitted."

D. Retention / legal hold
- We can accept 12 months for customer data with a carveout: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may retain aggregated telemetry, anonymized data, and administrative logs for up to eighteen (18) months solely for security, fraud detection and compliance. Redwood will not retain Customer personal data in identifiable form beyond the retention period except as required by law, in which case Redwood will notify Customer."

E. Subprocess matrix
- See attached redwood_subproc_matrix.csv. We'll commit to updating this list upon onboarding and will provide an automated notification to privacy@velaria.com.

Execution preference: DocuSign envelope (link below) — if Velaria requires AdobeSign we can accommodate but need a contact at procurement to ensure the envelope metadata matches the expected signatory flow.

DocuSign (proposed envelope): https://docusign.com/envelopes/ABC1234-velaria-dpa

Happy to hop on the Friday slot Hannah proposed.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference
